events.name: Safety Isn't Scary
events.description:
Safety Isn’t Scary is a haunted house event that will provide attendees with the opportunity to learn about safety strategies and resources at UF while also providing them a fun haunted house experience.

This event will be put on and organized by the Florida Greek Ambassadors, however, we will also be opening up delegate positions to those outside of the Florida Greek Ambassadors (but still members of the Greek community) who may want to help run, set up and advertise the event.

The date for the event will be on Sunday, October 18th. The event will be hosted from 7pm to 10pm at night with time dedicated before start to give tabling organizations time to set up.

This event will be hosted at the Delta Tau Delta fraternity house. We will be using their front lawn and downstairs rooms including their TV room, gym and dining room.

The event will consist of two sections, an outdoor section on the house front lawn for organizations to table at and the haunted house section inside the house. When a student arrives at the facility, they will be greeted at the entrance of the front lawn, asked to sign in and given a piece of paper with a certain number of boxes for signatures. Before being allowed to enter the haunted house, students must speak with and get the signatures of a certain number of organizations tabling at the event. Once they have done so, they will show the piece of paper to an FGA at the door who will then approve them for a tour. The haunted house tour will be done in groups of 3-4 people who will be escorted by an FGA for the duration of the tour.

We want to do this event because we believe that being safe is important throughout not just one’s college experience but their entire life. While it may seem counterintuitive, we think that by exposing attendees to fear, we are prepping them to think more about the resources they just learned about during the tabling section and hope to leave them with a more lasting impression.

In regards to the UF Greek Pillars, we believe this event most neatly fits into the Service and Community pillars. A safety event like this provides organizations the ability to spread their message and allows the community to learn more about and become more aware of these organizations. Ultimately, this exchange of ideas serves our students and creates a more connected, safety-conscious community.

In regards to the UF Division of Student Life’s Mission, we believe this event is most closely related to Lifelong Wellbeing and Community Connection. Safety is essential to someone’s wellbeing and by spreading this awareness we are fostering a greater connection between the community.

Women’s Ultimate is passionate about creating an inclusive student organization that promotes and values diversity. Our commitment to inclusion across race, gender, ethnicity, religion, or any other aspects that make our members unique is what allows our club to strengthen and grow. We do not tolerate any form of discrimination and strive to incorporate diversity, equity, and inclusion practices at the center of organization.

The UF Women's Ultimate Frisbee Club Team was founded 19 years ago, originally as "FUEL" (Florida Ultimate Elite Ladies).

The club includes both FUEL and our B-Team, DIESEL. Any UF student is welcome to come out and play and we guarantee you'll have a great time. There is a spot for everyone! The majority of people who come out have never played before.

Both teams compete in 4-6 tournaments a year against other schools, mostly in the southeast. However, FUEL has traveled as far as California, Texas, and Colorado in the last few years for competition.

We are funded by the University, which covers the majority of our costs.

FUEL qualified for Nationals in 2006, 2007, 2011, 2012, 2017 and 2018. In their seventh year, DIESEL is the only B-team to have qualified for and played in Regionals, and they've done so twice.

Come join us for practice and see what it's all about!

The UF Women's Ultimate Frisbee Club Team was founded in 2001, originally as "FUEL" (Florida Ultimate Elite Ladies).

The club includes both FUEL and our B-Team, DIESEL. Any UF student is welcome to come out and play and we guarantee you'll have a great time. There is a spot for everyone! The majority of people who come out have never played before.

Come join us for practice and see what it's all about!

events.name: SG Cabinet: Tech or Treat
events.description: Tech or Treat is a Halloween-themed tabling event hosted by the Emerging Technologies Cabinet to connect students with AI and emerging technology resources at UF. Students who stop by the table will spin a prize wheel that awards either a "Tech" goodie (such as phone chargers, phone wallets, portable fans, USB A to C adapters, or fidget toys) or a "Treat" (small, individually wrapped candy). There will also be a “jackpot” slot of the wheel with top tech prizes, with a choice between selecting a reliable portable charger or a keychain tracker (similar to AirTag). After receiving their prize, each student will have a brief conversation with the Cabinet Director or an Assistant Director about ways to get involved with AI and emerging technologies on campus. Every participant will also receive a printed pamphlet highlighting opportunities such as HiPerGator, the AI Scholars program, the AI² Center, CURBS, and other student organizations and university-affiliated programs. The event ran successfully last year, and this year's goal is to reach 75–125 students and increase awareness of the university's AI resources among students outside technical majors.

events.description:
Women’s Ultimate is passionate about creating an inclusive student organization that promotes and values diversity. Our commitment to inclusion across race, gender, ethnicity, religion, or any other aspects that make our members unique is what allows our club to strengthen and grow. We do not tolerate any form of discrimination and strive to incorporate diversity, equity, and inclusion practices at the center of organization.

The UF Women's Ultimate Frisbee Club Team was founded 19 years ago, originally as "FUEL" (Florida Ultimate Elite Ladies).

The club includes both FUEL and our B-Team, DIESEL. Any UF student is welcome to come out and play and we guarantee you'll have a great time. There is a spot for everyone! The majority of people who come out have never played before.

Both teams compete in 4-6 tournaments a year against other schools, mostly in the southeast. However, FUEL has traveled as far as California, Texas, and Colorado in the last few years for competition.

We are funded by the University, which covers the majority of our costs.

FUEL qualified for Nationals in 2006, 2007, 2011, 2012, 2017 and 2018. In their seventh year, DIESEL is the only B-team to have qualified for and played in Regionals, and they've done so twice.

Come join us for practice and see what it's all about!
